intro_md: 🎧 **10 min.** New listening, not the story again: Margaret and Nam talk over tea. You will hear how she met Peter and the advice she gives Nam. The words are hidden at first.

parts.title: Over tea: Margaret and Nam
parts.md:
![Tea with Margaret](data/img/w1/d14-tea.webp)

**Train your ears – the words are hidden at first:**
1. 👂 **Listen without the words.** Just follow. Missed a word? Keep going – the next sentence often explains it.
2. 👂 **Listen again**, still without the words. You'll catch more.
3. 📄 **Show transcript** – listen + read. **Tap any line** you missed to hear just that part again.
4. 👂 **Hide it** and listen one last time.

listen.text: On Saturday evening, Nam knocks on Margaret's door.
She has made tea and put out some biscuits.
Come in, dear. Sit by the window, that chair is the most comfortable.
Thank you for inviting me. I bought a bike today, by the way. It's outside.
A bike! Peter would have loved that. He was always fixing them.
Peter was your husband, right? I saw his photo in the hall.
Yes. We met because of a bike, actually. Mine had a flat tyre outside the hospital.
He walked past in a muddy coat and said, give me five minutes.
And he fixed it?
He did. Then he asked if he could buy me a coffee. I said no, and then I said yes.
How long were you together?
Forty years. He died six years ago, in the spring.
I'm so sorry, Margaret.
Thank you, dear. Some days are hard, but this street looks after me.
Did you ever think about moving somewhere quieter?
Never. Everyone I love lives within five minutes of this door.
Now, let me give you some advice. In your first year, say yes to every invitation.
Even when you're tired. Especially when you're tired.
I'll try. My sister Linh would agree with you, I think.
Tell me about her.
She's a teacher now, and she's brave and very funny. You would like her.
I'd love to meet her one day. Bring her to tea.
She'd like that. Now, who wants the last biscuit?
